page: Microsoft Azure M64m is an x86_64 memory-intensive server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 1792.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 28.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 7340 GB SSD, and virtualization is managed through Microsoft Hyper-V. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core workloads. Single-core performance is consistently low, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression tests all scoring in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core and parallelized execution metrics, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, fall within the middle 50% average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also register average performance.

Given the massive memory capacity and bundled 7340 GB SSD storage, this server is designed for memory-heavy workloads such as database operations and large-scale caching, with Redis SET operations and Passmark database benchmarks performing in the average tier. However, its weak single-core performance and poor text generation speeds in LLM inference make it less suitable for compute-heavy single-threaded tasks or real-time generative AI. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile represents a high-density memory allocation, trading raw CPU speed for massive RAM capacity and local SSD storage.
